A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 21-page documents, including supplementary Sections 6–7. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original deepfake-detection experiments, including cross-dataset evaluations, ablations, and robustness analyses in Tables 1–14.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–14, including the supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: The CLIP-based spatial and temporal decoder, Facial Component Guidance, training objectives, and inference procedure in Section 3 are unchanged. Abstract corrections do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same FF++, CDF, DFDC, FaceShifter, DeeperForensics, and diffusion-generated face evaluations, including missing-face and perturbation scenarios in the supplement.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding table, including the main detection baselines, CLIP linear probes, diffusion-image detectors, EVL comparison, and supplementary RealForensics comparisons.

E3.justification: Training settings, dataset splits, preprocessing, AUROC/AP metrics, leave-one-out protocols, training-data proportions, and supplementary perturbation procedures are identical.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component and attribute ablations, data-efficiency experiments, attention visualization, missing-face evaluation, augmentation analyses, and image/video robustness tests.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–14 and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same 92.6 average AUROC and 81.2 DFDC AUROC for Ours(ViT-L/14), versus 91.7 and 76.8 for TALL-Swin.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–5, and supplementary attention-extraction Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and generalization claims, including the reported 0.9-point average AUROC advantage and 4.4-point DFDC advantage. Wording corrections do not change their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning facial guidance, temporal inconsistencies, dataset-specific cues, data efficiency, and robustness are unchanged, including supplementary qualifications about missing faces and perturbations.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and the supplement retain identical preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time estimates, data details, and software links. The author-email edit adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to previous methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes duplicated abstract wording and repairs malformed words such as 'guidencourage', 'improvementsuccess', 'especiallytablishing', and the introduction's 'improvementmargin'. One author email and the version/date stamp also change; section organization remains identical.

P2.justification: The corrected abstract and introduction undergo limited text reflow, with the abstract becoming slightly shorter. Figures 1–3, Tables 1–14, their captions and placement, and rendered pages 3–21 remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 removes conspicuous duplicated wording and malformed words from the abstract and introduction, improving readability of the paper's central summary. The scientific content, experimental evidence, and supplementary material remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited to editorial quality.
